title: Where does your work become structurally yours?
question: For the work you have now, what have you built, what travels with you, who decides, and what could continue if the container changed?

claims.text: What exists because this person made it exist?
claims.storyQuote: What exists because this person made it exist?

claims.text: Look for a recognizable body of work, methods, relationships, audience, and operating capacity, not merely output or attention.
claims.storyQuote: Look for a recognizable body of work, methods, relationships, audience, and operating capacity, not merely output or attention.

claims.text: What survives when the container changes?
claims.storyQuote: What survives when the container changes?

claims.text: Look for capability, reputation, systems, relationships, and opportunities that can travel across an employer, platform, client, format, or moment.
claims.storyQuote: Look for capability, reputation, systems, relationships, and opportunities that can travel across an employer, platform, client, format, or moment.

claims.text: Who can decide what happens next?
claims.storyQuote: Who can decide what happens next?

claims.text: Look for meaningful authority over identity, access, rights, revenue, data, and the conditions under which the work is used.
claims.storyQuote: Look for meaningful authority over identity, access, rights, revenue, data, and the conditions under which the work is used.

claims.text: What could persist if an essential dependency changed?
claims.storyQuote: What could persist if an essential dependency changed?

claims.text: Look for work, systems, relationships, or authority that could keep functioning if a role, platform, employer, client, or other essential dependency changed.
claims.storyQuote: Look for work, systems, relationships, or authority that could keep functioning if a role, platform, employer, client, or other essential dependency changed.

claims.text: If the role disappeared, the platform changed its rules, the distributor walked away, or the employer kept the system, what work, systems, relationships, or authority could continue?
claims.storyQuote: If the role disappeared, the platform changed its rules, the distributor walked away, or the employer kept the system, what work, systems, relationships, or authority could continue?

claims.text: The model should therefore produce a map of relationships, not a halo.
claims.storyQuote: The model should therefore produce a map of relationships, not a halo.

claims.text: It does not certify that a person has crossed a binary threshold or earned an institutional status.
claims.storyQuote: It does not certify that a person has crossed a binary threshold or earned an institutional status.

claims.text: No private contract, cap table, or participant interview was reviewed for this edition.
claims.storyQuote: No private contract, cap table, or participant interview was reviewed for this edition.

claims.text: The counts under your map add up to the marks you made. Nothing is weighted.
claims.derivation: number of items carrying each mark

shows: Your own list, sorted under the edition’s four questions in your words
Which items you mark as staying with you, going with the container or not sure, for each of the edition’s four changes
doesNotShow: A score, a grade or a verdict. The map lists and counts what you marked and nothing else.
Whether you own, may keep or may reuse any item. The map holds your answers and does not check a contract, a platform’s terms or a record.
Who you are like. The edition’s cases are not matched to your answers.
